title: Skills & agent roles
summary: Start with a repeatable task, then choose procedures and specialist guidance that fit your work.

sections.label: Start with the task
sections.text: Investigate requirements, assess a change, diagnose a pipeline failure, verify data or prepare evidence. The procedure names the work. Its specialization supplies details for a particular environment.

sections.label: Procedure, skill and role
sections.text: A reading procedure explains how to approach a task. An exported skill packages supported instructions for reuse. A role names responsibility and boundaries. A topic is not automatically an exportable skill or a working tool connection.

sections.label: Reusable entry points
sections.text: Diagnose a pipeline failure, Verify data and query results, and Verify sources and evidence are general starting points below. Jenkins, RDF/SPARQL and country-source review keep their specialist detail within explicit scopes.

sections.label: Author from evidence
sections.text: Create a skill when a useful procedure repeats or an observed failure reveals missing guidance. Supply actual inputs, expected outputs and acceptance checks. Confirm the fit of the procedure before using it in your environment.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
sections.text: Choose repeatable task procedures while designing the approach, then assign scoped procedure outputs and role responsibilities in the delivery plan. The existing skill reference is retained. This gap review does not install skills, audit every host capability or establish that an example matches the current workplace.

sections.label: Gap review: acceptance outputs
items: A task-to-procedure list records the repeated job or observed failure each proposed skill addresses.
The plan distinguishes a reading guide, supported exportable skill, specialist example and role assignment.
Each selected procedure has actual required inputs, a reviewable output and acceptance owner, with host support unresolved where untested.

catalog.applicability: Use this cluster to distinguish reusable task procedures, specialist reading examples and supported generated instructions.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
